review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definition file Def_AlgebraicGeometry_OrderedAffineCoverCechOrdered.lean, which holds ores_apply, od_apply, oext_apply_*, ounitPullback_apply and osort_val. I grepped for downstream uses of ores_oext, ores_od and ores_ocup. None of the relevant lemmas are tagged @[simp], and every proof and downstream use rewrites them by hand with rw. I did not check whether other simp lemmas (for example sign_refl) would interact with the proposed attributes. I could not run Lean, so I make no claim about loops or simp failures. The proposed orientations push ores inward and shrink terms, so I expect no cycle.

findings.excerpt: F.ores K n (F.oext K n z) = z
findings.problem: ores_oext is a retraction identity (ores ∘ oext = id) that rewrites a composite to a smaller term, so it fits the simp normal form. ores_od and ores_ocup likewise push `ores` through `od` and `ocup` to their non-ordered versions `d` and `cup`. None of the three is tagged @[simp] or registered in a simp set. Downstream code applies them one at a time, for example `rw [ores_ocup, ores_oext, ores_oext]` and `rw [map_sub, orev_oext, hrev, map_sub, ores_oext, map_zsmul, ...]`. This means a user cannot let simp normalise `ores (oext z)`, and each use needs the exact rewrite order spelled out.
findings.proposed_change: Mark ores_oext @[simp]. It has a plain left-hand side and no side conditions. Consider @[simp] on ores_od and ores_ocup as well, since their right-hand sides are `d` and `cup`. This is a normal form for ordered-to-alternating cochains and each rule strictly removes an `o`-operation. Because the lemmas sit inside `DORDProofs` and are reused through exported wrappers, put the attributes on the exported theorems, or on the definition-file versions if moved there. Then downstream steps like the `rw [ores_ocup, ores_oext, ores_oext]` call can be `simp only [ores_ocup, ores_oext]`, or plain `simp`.
findings.benefit: Callers that combine `ores` with `oext`, `od` and `ocup` get a canonical normal form. They would no longer repeat `rw [ores_oext, ores_oext]` or depend on the order of rewrites. Chains that rewrite under `map_sub` or `map_zsmul` would also become simp calls.

findings.declaration: ores_oext, ores_ounitPullback_oext, od_ounitPullback (use of ores_apply, od_apply, oext_apply_of_not_injective)
findings.problem: The definitional unfolding lemmas ores_apply, od_apply, ounitPullback_apply, oext_apply_of_injective and oext_apply_of_not_injective are not simp lemmas, so the proofs rewrite them manually. The file works around the missing simp coverage with long `change` blocks that restate the unfolded terms. An example is `change (X.presheaf.map _).hom ((h.app _).hom (0 : Γ(Y, ...))) = ...`. The lemmas are stated with `rfl` or `simp only` proofs and have clear oriented forms. `ores_apply : F.ores K n c s = c s.1` is a projection-style rewrite and is non-looping. `oext_apply_of_not_injective` has the hypothesis `¬ Function.Injective t`, which simp can discharge from a local `hinj`.
findings.proposed_change: In the definition file, mark `ores_apply` @[simp]. Mark `oext_apply_of_not_injective` @[simp] too. Its right-hand side is `0` and its side condition is a hypothesis that `simp [hinj]` can discharge. Keep `od_apply` and `ounitPullback_apply` as explicit `simp only` or `rw` lemmas. Their right-hand sides expand into sums and presheaf maps, so a global simp tag could cause unwanted expansion. Then the not-injective branch of ores_ounitPullback_oext could be closed by `simp [ores_apply, oext_apply_of_not_injective _ _ _ _ _ hinj, unitPullback_apply_of_not_injective ...]` instead of an explicit `change` and `rw [map_zero, map_zero]`.
findings.benefit: `ores` applied to an ordered cochain then reduces automatically to evaluation at `s.1`, and the zero branch of `oext` is handled by hypothesis discharge. This removes the need for hand-written `change` statements in the degenerate (non-injective) case.
